notes: Not checked here: the real browser microphone (getUserMedia, ScriptProcessor, real AudioContext at 16 kHz), real WebSocket timing, and rendering in a real browser. T8.7 owns that. Judgement on transcript/card after deleted: the client accepts them and shows them (reproduced at Session level; App.tsx renders turns and card with no check on connection). I did not fail it because the contract says the server answers deleted and closes, so a conforming server cannot send them, and the real backend (T8.2) is not present to show it can. In a privacy-focused product it is cheap hardening, though: ignore transcript and card when connection is deleting, deleted or closed. Recommend T8.7 or T8.2 verify the real server cannot emit a late transcript after deleted (background ingest), and add the client guard if it can. Also: (a) a server error status while recording leaves the microphone live and sending audio while the indicator says 'Error', so the indicator under-reports a live microphone; a press-time error such as as_of_seq will do this until the next press. (b) The sendAudio connection guard and the stop() track-stop are unprotected by tests: removing the guard or the stopTracks() call in stop() leaves all 44 tests passing. The code is correct as written. (c) contract.test.ts covers outgoing frames only. (d) Ajv runs with strict:false and ignores the 'discriminator' keyword; shape-based oneOf makes this safe.
